Commentary.Commentary: So, that will be all from this series! With this win, England bag another 30 points in the ICC World Test Championship and takes their total to 146 points. They have won the series 3-1 away from home and this will give a lot of confidence to a young English team who are gaining valuable experience. As for South Africa, the pressure continues to mount on skipper Faf du Plessis as his side fail to deliver and are losing by huge margins. They will need huge improvements in the coming months so that their transition can become smoother. For now, that is it from our side. Do join us for the ODI series that starts from the 4th of February, 2020. That game begins at 1300 Local (1100 GMT). Until then, cheers and take care!

Joe Root, the victorious England skipper, says that this is a very special series win and he is very proud of the boys and thanks the crowd for coming out in large numbers. Says that the retirement of players is opportunities for others and the sky is the limit for them. Says he is excited with the team coming through as many of them are at the start of their careers. Adds that they expected fierce competition against the South Africans and they were not disappointed. Thanks them for their hospitality and all that they have done for them.

MAN OF THE SERIES IS BEN STOKES for his incredible performances with bat, ball and in fielding as well. He starts by saying the most important thing is to win and that they walk away with a series victory and he hopes that this award brings a smile on his father's face. Says it is always a very competitive series against the South African's and he just enjoys playing against them. Credits Ollie Pope, Dominic Sibley, Zak Crawley and Sam Curran as they consistently stand up and deliver.

MAN OF THE MATCH IS MARK WOOD for his amazing performances with the ball. Says he was a bit of a doubt coming into the game but now he is over the moon. Says he has had a lot of dark days but the physios have helped him out very much along with his teammates and the crowd. Says the only advice that he can give to anyone is that give all that they have.

South African skipper, Faf du Plessis, says that they played well in the first Test but says that England were better than them from thereon, both with bat and ball. Says that Nortje has been a shining light for them and it is difficult to replace the likes of Morne Morkel. Also credits Hendricks for his 5-fer. Says that they did not bat well but Rassie played very well against a very good England attack. Credits Vernon Philander on his retirement as he is a champion on and off the pitch and he is sad that he could not give him the send off he deserves. Adds that he deserves everything he gets for a decade of service which he has given to Cricket South Africa.

Mike Haysman is down for the presentation ceremony. First up, he calls Vernon Philander as he is given a token of appreciation for his services to South African Cricket. Vernon Philander says this is not the way he wanted to end his career but credits the English team for the way they played. On the appreciation Philander received from the English players, he says they are all gentleman at the end of the game and he thanks his teammates as well as Cricket South Africa. Ends by saying that he plans to stay in cricket and he wants to mentor the young guys coming through and contribute as much as he can.

Earlier in the match, England outplayed South Africa as they powered their way to a score of 400 runs. The opening stand of Crawley and Sibley provided the foundation and the last wicket stand between Broad and Woakes added 82 runs of immense value. Nortje performed brilliantly as he came out with a 5-fer to his name. South Africa in reply scored a meager 183 runs. Quinton de Kock played an innings which saved his team from embarrassment as he scored 76 runs. Mark Wood picked up a 5-fer in the first innings and he ran through the Proteas' batting line-up. Woakes and Stokes chipped in with a couple of wickets each while Curran took one wicket. England did not enforce the follow-on and opted to bat. However, they did not play well with only skipper Joe Root scoring more than 50 runs as they finished on 248. Debutant Beuran Hendricks bowled superbly to bag a 5-fer and give his team a slim chance in the game.

The bowling from England was not superb in the first two sessions but they were persistent and they got their rewards exactly at the right times as well. The wicket of Dean Elgar right before Lunch was a setback for the Proteas. However, the biggest blow for the South Africans came when Faf du Plessis and Rassie van der Dussen departed in consecutive overs and from there on it was all England. The pick of the bowlers was Mark Wood as he picked up a 4-fer, taking the main wicket of Rassie van der Dussen. Ben Stokes took the crucial wickets of Elgar and du Plessis while Stuart Broad also chipped in with a couple of wickets. Woakes picked up a wicket as well.

The day started on a positive note for the South Africans as Pieter Malan and Dean Elgar looked strong for the first hour but Malan then departed. Elgar and Rassie van der Dussen formed a 60-run stand but then Elgar lost his wicket too just before the Lunch break. The most promising time for the Proteas came when Rassie van der Dussen and skipper Faf du Plessis were batting and stitched a 92-run stand. However, Stokes dismissed the South African skipper and that opened the floodgates for them. Van der Dussen played a brilliant knock of 98 runs but it went in vain as he departed soon after his skipper. After the Tea break, it was almost inevitable that England would win. Bavuma and de Kock played some strokes to cheer the fans up as they made a 48-run stand but once Bavuma departed, South Africa collapsed from 235/4 to 274 all out.

What a performance this has been from the English team! After losing the first Test match, they have bounced back in fantastic style and inflicted a defeat that has emphasized the flaws of this South African team. However, defeating any team at their home in such convincing fashion is always good and this will give England a lot of confidence.

OUT! CAUGHT! ENGLAND HAVE WON THE MATCH! Nortje is the last man to depart. Wood takes the final one. Not the best of the balls but England and Root will take it. Wood bowls one down the leg side. Nortje looks to go for a fine tickle but fails to do so as it goes to Buttler. The England players immediately go up in appeal but the umpire is unmoved. Root immediately signals the 'T' and the replays roll in. Ultra Edge shows that there was a spike as the ball went past Nortje's glove. The umpire reverses his decision and that will be all. ENGLAND SEAL THE SERIES 3-1!

Review time! Root wants to go upstairs for a caught behind against Nortje. It looks out to the naked eye. Replays show Wood is fine on the front foot. The Ultra Edge comes in and spots a faint edge off the gloves.
Short ball on middle and leg, Nortje ducks under it.
Dane Paterson is the last man in for South Africa.

OUT! RUN OUT! Disaster strikes and that is a shambles as Hendricks departs now. Full ball on middle and leg, Nortje plays this one down to mid on and sets off for a run. Hendricks does not have eyes for his partner and is ball-watching. Nortje has reached the non-striker end and Hendricks is at the same end as well. Hendricks runs towards the striker's end but Sibley at mid on collects the ball and has the presence of mind to throw the ball at the striker's end. Buttler collects the ball and whips the bails off with Hendricks well short. England just a wicket away from victory!
On the pads, worked towards square leg for a couple.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Just about misses the leg pole. Root floats it up on off, Hendricks looks to play at it but the ball goes off the inside edge past the leg pole and towards fine leg and the batters take a couple.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Tossed up on off, defended by Hendricks.
A short delivery which has been pulled away. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Back of a length ball on middle, Hendricks pulls but straight to the man at square leg.
Way wide down the leg side, Hendricks goes after it but misses.
On middle and off, pushed towards the man at mid off.
Back of a length ball on middle and leg, defended by Hendricks by getting up on his toes.
Beauran Hendricks walks in to bat on debut. How long can the pair of Hendricks and Nortje keep England at bay?

OUT! CAUGHT! Chris Woakes takes the catch and this has to be the final nail in the coffin for South Africa. Back of a length ball on middle and off, Quinton de Kock looks to pull but he only manages to get a top edge on this one. The ball goes up in the air towards mid off where Chris Woakes runs across and takes the catch. De Kock throws his wicket away and England heading to a comfortable victory.
De Kock drives this through the covers. One run added to the total.

A loud appeal for LBW but it has been turned down. Root bowls a slider on off and middle, de Kock is late in bringing his bat down in time. The ball struck him high om the pads there. The English players appeal but the umpire is unmoved. Maybe, it hit the batsman high.
Tossed up on off, Nortje plays the reverse sweep and gets a single.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Floated on off, blocked out.
Tossed up on off, Anrich prods forward and defends.
FOUR! Whatever happens at the other end, de Kock looks unfazed! Length ball outside off, de Kock rocks back and cuts this one through the point region for a boundary.

Shouts of catch it but no one there! Length ball on middle, Nortje looks to work this one towards the leg side but the ball goes off the leading edge uppishly towards cover-point but there is no one there and the batters take one.
Length ball on off, Nortje defends it out.
Length ball on middle and off, defended by Nortje.
Anrich Nortje is the new man in.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! Philander departs and the whole crowd stands up and applauds the great man. He raises his bat as he accepts the applause and walks down the tunnel being a proud man having given his all for the nation. Back of a length ball down the leg side, Philander looks to tickle it fine down the leg side but he gets a faint edge on that and Buttler does well as he dives low to his left and takes the catch. The England players appeal and the umpire raises his dreaded finger. England 3 wickets away from the victory.
Bouncer on middle and leg, Philander looks to hook but misses.

SIX! A huge one and first one of the innings for Quinton de Kock! Floated delivery on middle and off, de Kock goes down on one knee and this time connects with his slog sweep as he sends this delivery into the stands at the mid-wicket region.
De Kock has played this one towards the man at mid on.
The batsman opens the face of the bat and helps it to third man.
Philander pushes this one down towards the leg side and takes a single.
Another one on the pads, defended out.
Floated on middle and leg, defended towards the leg side.
FOUR! Stand and deliver from Quinton de Kock! Full delivery on middle and off, de Kock just smashes this one over mid on for a boundary.
Length ball on the hips, Philander looks to pull but the ball goes off the inner half towards the leg side and the batters take a single.
Philander goes back in his crease and defends this one out.
FOUR! Another back of a length ball on middle, Philander rocks back and now pulls it in front of square leg for a boundary.
FOUR! Philander is off the mark in style in his final test innings! Length ball outside off, Philander rocks back and cuts this one through the point region for a boundary.
Length delivery on middle and off, defended.
Mark Wood is back into the attack. 13-3-34-1, his figures so far.
Tossed up delivery on off, defended towards the off side.
Again de Kock drives towards the cover region but finds the man there.
Flatter one on off, defended by de Kock.
Tossed up ball outside off, de Kock tries to go for the slog sweep but misses it as the ball spins away.
Floated on off again, pushed to the man at cover.
Floated on off, driven towards the man at cover.
Joe Root is back on. 3-0-23-0, his figures so far.
Length ball on middle and leg, Philander looks to flick but misses to get hit on the thigh pad.
Length ball outside off, de Kock plays an exquisite square cut but it goes straight to the man in the deep and the batters take a single.
Vernon Philander walks out to bat for his final Test match. The whole crowd stands up and applauds the man for his achievements.

OUT! CAUGHT! Stuart Broad is a tall man and it is very difficult hooking him and Pretorius departs in that very attempt! Bouncer on middle and leg, Pretorius goes back and looks to pull but gets a top edge on that one. It goes towards backward square leg where Sam Curran runs in and takes a very good catch diving forward. England 4 wickets away from the win.
Outside off, left alone.
Bouncer on middle and off, Pretorius does well to sway away from that.
On the pads, worked towards square leg for a single.
Pretorius shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Another one outside off, left alone.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Length ball outside off, moving away, Pretorius shuffles but lets it be.
This time on the pads of Pretorius, he flicks this one towards mid-wicket and takes a couple. He is off the mark with this.
Good length ball on the pads, de Kock looks to flick but misses to get hit on the pads. De Kock crosses for a leg bye as the ball rolls towards the leg side.
Dwaine Pretorius walks in to bat next.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! Bavuma has to depart and that is a cracking nut by Broad! Broad bowls a bouncer on middle and off, Bavuma hops and first thinks about playing at it but then realises that it is too high. He tries to drop his hands but by then the ball goes off his gloves and into the mitts of Buttler who takes an easy catch. Broad gets his first wicket of the Test match and he has shown his class against the youngster. Half the side back in the hut for South Africa.

FOUR! Super shot from Bavuma! Back of a length ball on off, Bavuma has driven cut that one through the point region and the ball has raced away to the fence. Partnership moves to 48 runs with this one off just 51 balls.
The batsman defends it from within the crease. One run added to the total.
FOUR! Driven away! Full ball on middle and leg, de Kock has driven this one down the ground through mid on for a boundary.
On the hips, de Kock looks to flick but is hit on the thigh pad instead.
Full ball on middle, played towards the man at mid on.
Stuart Broad is back on. 8-1-15-0, his figures so far.

EDGED AND FOUR! Bavuma flirting with danger here. Almost a bouncer on off, Bavuma hops and looks to cut. The ball goes off the edge and above the man at third slip and into the third man fence. Matter of inches there and Stokes would be wishing that he was standing there instead of his skipper to add those extra inches.
Bouncer on middle and leg, Bavuma ducks under it.
On off again, this time de Kock plays it towards point for a single.
Length ball on off, pushed towards cover for a single.

FOUR! Smashed away! South Africa not hiding anymore! Back of a length ball on middle, Bavuma rocks back and pulls this uppishly towards square leg and the ball crosses the ropes on a couple of bounces.
Back of a length ball on middle, defended by Bavuma.
Back of a length ball outside off, de Kock goes for the cut but edges it in the process. The ball rolls towards the slip cordon.

FOUR! Back to back boundaries. De Kock is showing his class here. He is not going to give up there. He comes on the front foot to this pitched up ball and drives it srisply through covers. Not a fielder moved as the ball met the fence.
FOUR! Pulled with disdain. Woakes goes short and on middle, de Kock pulls it off the back foot into the gap at mid-wicket to find the fence.
Full and on middle, de Kock drives it with a straight bat towards mid on.
Another back of a length ball on off, chopped towards point.

The ball is being checked by the umpires for its shape. The 8-shaped gauge is out and yes, it is not going through one of the sides. The ball will be changed and an official is out with a box of the Kookaburras. Finally, the ball has been changed and play will resume.
Good length and on off, pushed to mid off.
FOUR! Back of a length ball on off, Bavuma punches it past point and the ball races to the fence behind.
BEATEN! Back of length ball on off, Bavuma looks to punch it off the back foot the ball bounces a bit more and goes past the outside edge.
Back of a length ball on middle, Bavuma flicks it towards fine leg. The fielder there was much squarer and that allows the batsmen to take a couple.
Bavuma looks to flick this back of a length ball to mid-wicket but the ball goes towards mid on.
Length delivery outside off, Bavuma lifts his bat and lets it go.
Length ball outside off, Quinton drives this one towards cover-point and gets to the other end.
Another one outside off, Bavuma does not fiddle with it.
Outside off, Temba leaves it alone.

FOUR! This time an educational edge! Length ball outside off, Bavuma looks to guide this towards third man but it goes finer than he expected and the ball races away to the fence. 200 comes up for South Africa with this.
FOUR! Creamed! Full ball on off, Bavuma drives this one beautifully through the cover region for a boundary. Gets off the mark with probably the shot of the day!
Another back of a length ball on off, this time de Kock plays it in the gap at point and takes a single.
Back of a length ball outside off, de Kock plays this one towards the point fielder.
Length ball outside off, Bavuma guides this one towards the man at point.
Outside off, Temba does not bother to play at it.
On the pads of Bavuma, he works this one towards the leg side.
Outside off, Bavuma does not fiddle with it.
Another back of a length ball, Bavuma looks to defend but the ball hits his glove and falls down on the leg side.
Length ball on off, Bavuma rocks back and blocks.
Length ball on middle and off, defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.

EDGED AND FOUR! Lucky break for Quinton de Kock! A length ball, pitching and angling away from de Kock. He looks to defend but the ball goes off the outside edge between third slip and gully and the ball races away to the fence.
Full ball on the off pole line, de Kock defends it off the front foot onto the ground.
Good length ball on the off pole line by Woakes, de Kock defends it.
This time a fuller ball on the middle and leg pole line, played towards the man at mid-wicket.
Good length ball on middle and off, to start with by Woakes, de Kock blocks it out.

Welcome back for the final session of Day 4. South Africa after battling out the second session collapsed in the few overs before the Tea interval. Quinton de Kock and Temba Bavuma walk in to resume the South African chase. Whereas, England players are out on the field with a new vigour. Chris Woakes will start the session with the ball.
... Day 4, Session 3 ...

The session started smoothly for South Africa as Rassie van der Dussen counter-attacked everything thrown at him whereas skipper Faf du Plessis grinding out his whole innings. They both combined to stitch a 92-run stand and everything was looking positive for South Africa. However, Ben Stokes came and once again provided the pivotal breakthrough of Faf du Plessis which shook the confidence of South Africa. In the very next over, Rassie van der Dussen fell after a brilliant innings and that has now opened the floodgates for England. Two new batters in the form of Quinton de Kock and Temba Bavuma are at the crease with the latter looking shakier than ever. Join us for the last session of Day 4 and possibly the whole series at 1530 Local (1330 GMT) as England will be looking to come out all guns blazing!

Another session comes to an end and England have struck gold right in the latter stages. For once it looked like South Africa were staging a comeback in this game and in this series but it all fell apart as Stokes and Wood shattered the dreams of the South African team.
Length ball outside off, Bavuma leaves it to see of the session. TEA ON DAY4!
Length ball outside off, Bavuma plays it with an angled bat towards gully.
Full outside off, Bavuma shoulders arms to it.
Back of a length ball on middle and leg, de Kock tucks it towards fine leg and rotates the strike.
Short ball on off, Quinton lets it go through.
Length and outside off, de Kock lets it be.
Outside off, pushed towards covers.
Length and outside off, left alone by Bavuma.

Lucky man! Bavuma is lucky not to lob this to the close in fielder. Bouncer on middle and leg, he looks to flicks it off the back foot but the ball goes off the glove and lobs wide of short leg and short of backward square leg. The fielder there looks interested a bit but the ball drops in front of him.
Outside off, left alone.
Temba Bavuma is the new man in.

OUT! CAUGHT! The nervous 90s bug has bitten Rassie van der Dussen as he takes a long walk back to the dressing room. He looks dejected. Rassie was expecting some chin music there with the field spread out. However, Wood surprises him with a full ball on off. Seeing the length, van der Dussen's eyes lit up and he goes for the expansive cover drive. He does not time it perfectly and it goes a touch uppishly to the right of Stuart Broad who tumbles low in that direction to take a good catch. Wood deserves this wicket more than anyone as he has been bowling well all day. Van der Dussen misses his ton by two runs and England get two wickets in two overs.
Back of a length ball on middle, Rassie plays it to mid-wicket.
Good length ball on middle and off, defended back towards the bowler.
On the pads, worked towards the leg side for a single.
FOUR! Good comeback by Rassie van der Dussen! Full ball on the middle and leg pole line, van der Dussen drives this one straight back down the ground through mid on for a boundary.

Another one which was almost chopped on! This is Ben Stokes at his best! Bouncer just outside off, van der Dussen looks to hop and defend. The ball goes off the inside edge onto the turf again but this time past the stumps. Van der Dussen survives and England smelling blood here.
Back of a length ball on off, Quinton de Kock punches this ball off the back foot towards cover for a single. Gets off the mark!
Quinton de Kock walks into bat. South Africa's hopes relies on him now. Can he script something special in this innings?

OUT! CHOPPED ON! Faf du Plessis departs after a fighting knock but for England, Ben Stokes is the man yet again! Stokes bowls a length ball just around off, it pitches and nips back in a bit. It also hits the crack and that makes the ball stay low. Faf du Plessis looks to come forward and defend but the ball goes off the bottom edge, onto the turf and then onto the middle pole to dislodge the bails. The skipper departs and a huge, huge blow for the Proteas!
Another ill-directed bouncer, Rassie lets it go.
The physio is out in the middle and is giving treatment to Rassie van der Dussen.

Ouch! That might have sent shivers down the spine of Rassie van der Dussen. Wood goes short and directed on the body. Rassie looks to leave it by dropping hos wrists but the ball does not bounce as expected and it hits his chest hard. Rassie is onto his knees as he waits for the physio to attend to him.
Length and on off, pushed to the off side off the back foot.
Length and on off, pushed to cover off the back foot.

EDGED AND FOUR! That was an educational edge there. Rassie van der Dussen moves into the nervous 90s. He looks to keep out this length ball outside off but the ball just about manages to take the outside edge and fall short off the diving gully fielder. The ball goes past him and into the fence at third man.
Short ball but wayward. Rassie ducks it.
Back of a length ball on middle, Faf hops inside the crease and defends it towards mid on.
Back of a length ball on off, Faf blocks it off the back foot.
Good length and outside off, Faf is in no mood to touch it.
Full and on  the pads, Rassie flicks it towards fine leg and gets to the other end.
Length and outside off, left alone.
FOUR! Length ball outside off, van der Dussen cuts it off the back foot through cover-point and the ball runs to the fence at deep point.
Ben Stokes is back on. 9-3-16-1, his figures so far.
Outside off, kept out off the back foot.
Length ball outside off,Faf punches it off the back foot towards covers where Broad dives to his left and fields it.
Faf is happy to defend it towards covers off the back foot.
Faf flicks it off the back foot towards mid-wicket.
Full and on off, Faf defends it by going low.
FOUR! Du Plessis sees the length early and flicks it off his pads. The ball rolls all along the ground towards mid-wicket for a boundary.
Tossed up on off, pushed to covers.
Outside off, defended to the off side.
Run off a misfield! Faf drives this full ball straight towards mid off where the fielder slides and parries it towards long on. The batsmen take a run.
Floated ball on off, Faf tucks it towards mid-wicket.
Tossed up on off, Faf drives it to find mid off to perfection.
Full on off, pushed to covers.
Length and on the pads, Faf tucks it to square leg and takes a run.
Another bumper in the over but down the leg side. Faf does not fiddle with it.
Length ball on off, Faf looks to defend it off the back foot. The ball bounces a bit extra and pings du Plessis on the glove. He loses his grip on the bat too as he throws it away.
Well-directed short ball, Faf sits under it.
Full and on off, Rassie drives it towards covers for a single.
Back of a length ball on off, Rassie hops and defends it from the crease.
The batsman dances down the track but decides to defend it. Good over for the Proteas again.
Van der Dussen pushes this one towards the mid on region and takes a single.
Floated on off, defended towards cover.
Tossed up on off, pushed towards cover.
FOUR! A freebie by Denly and it has been hit away! Full toss on middle, van der Dussen dances down the track and he has smashed that down to the long on fence for a boundary.
Floated on off, pushed towards cover for a single.
Full on the pads, flicked towards mid-wicket.
Full and on the off stump, Rassie defends it off the front foot towards the off side.
Short ball on middle, Rassie ducks under it.
Length ball on off, Rassie looks to lay bat on ball but it sneaks past the outside edge.
Length ball on off, pushed towards covers.
Length ball on off, Faf tucks it to mid-wicket for a run.
FOUR! Brilliantly done. Van der Dussen dances down once again and drives this towards long on for a boundary.
SIX! Tossed up on off, van der Dussen dances down the wicket and lofts this over the cow corner fence for a biggie.
Faf now drives this full ball towards mid on for a single.
Faf drives this full ball towards long on for a single.
Tossed up on off, driven towards covers.
Full on the off stump, Rassie pushes it towards covers and gets to the other end.
Joe Denly to try his luck and break this stand with his leg spin after the break.

Drinks Break! South Africa are not there yet but they are slowly and gently putting up a fight. Rassie van der Dussen is looking excellent out in the middle and is unbeaten at 67. Faf du Plessis is fighting it out and is helping South African fans dream. England need to break this stand, yes they have a lot of runs but they would not want to play close to the fire.
Full ball on off, played straight to the man at cover.
Length ball just around off, du Plessis defends it onto the pitch.
Good length ball on middle and off, pushed back towards the cover region.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Pushed to the cover region by the batsman. They pick up a single.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Mark Wood to have another burst.
Length ball on middle and leg, du Plessis plays it back to the bowler.

Length ball on middle and off, defended back towards the bowler.

EDGED AND FOUR! Length ball on off, du Plessis looks to drive but the ball goes off the outside edge through the slip cordon and the gully fielder for a boundary. 50-run stand comes up with this boundary.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Full ball on off, pushed towards cover for a single.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Another one on the pads, again Faf looks to flick but misses.
Length ball on middle and off, du Plessis looks to flick but misses to get hit on the thigh pad. The England players put in an appeal but it is waived away by the umpire.

On the pads, flicked towards square leg for a single.
Good length ball on middle and off, defended towards the man at mid off.
Good length and on off, Rassie leaves it alone.
Full on the pads, Rassie flicks it to mid-wicket.
FOUR! Beautifully played that! Full and outside off, Rassie van der Dussen drives it off the front foot. The ball goes behind square on the off side and rolls to the fence  there.
Length and on off, driven towards covers.
Full and on the pads, Faf flicks it to get an inside edge onto the pads. The ball rolls towards fine leg and the batsmen cross ends.
Length and angling into the batsman. Faf defends it back to the bowler.
Back of a length ball on middle, van der Dussen defends it off the back foot.
On the pads, du Plessis has worked it off his pads behind square. One run added to the total.
Length ball on middle and off, du Plessis looks to defend but misses.
Outside off, left alone.
Good length ball on middle and off, du Plessis looks to defend but gets an inside edge on it. The ball rolls just past the off pole and misses by a whisker.
Length ball on middle and off, defended off the back foot onto the pitch.
On the pads works this one towards the leg side.
Van der Dussen has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.

Length ball outside off, van der Dussen looks to defend but fails to do so. It hits something and lobs towards the slip cordon where the fielder comes forward, takes the catch and appeals. The umpire shakes his head. Replays roll in to show that this had hit the thigh pad.
Full ball on middle and off, van der Dussen drives this one towards cover but Sibley there makes a superb diving stop.
Good length ball on off, pushed towards cover-point for a single.
Sam Curran is on now. 8-2-23-0 are his figures so far.
Length and on off, pushed back to the bowler off the front foot.
Full on the pads, van der Dussen flicks it straight to the man at mid-wicket.
Full and outside off, brilliantly driven but superbly fielded at covers by Dominic Sibley.
Full on off, driven towards mid on.
Full on off, Rassie drives this towards covers and shouts a loud no.
Back of a length ball on off, Rassie hops and defends it to the leg side.
Length delivery on off, Faf pushes it to covers.
Good length on off, pushed to mid on off the back foot.
Length and outside off, Faf presents the full face off the bat as he blocks it off the front foot.
Length and on off, Faf looks to push this ball but he gets an inside edge onto the boots and the ball rolls towards point.
Length ball outside off, left alone.
Good length ball on off, played towards point for a single.
Good length ball just outside off, Rassie looks to work it towards the leg side but the ball goes off the outside edge towards gully for a single.
Another one which stays low after hitting the crack! Short delivery around off, the ball pitches and stays low to hit Rassie van der Dussen on the hips as he hops and looks to defend.
Full ball on middle and off, driven towards the man at mid on.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Full ball on off, pushed towards cover for a single.
Bouncer on middle, a fierce one, du Plessis does well to sway away from it.
Good length ball on middle and off, van der Dussen looks to defend but the ball goes off the inside edge and onto the pads.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Rassie van der Dussen has now been hit on the glove. Not too bad though as he continues.

Down the leg side, du Plessis looks to flick this one towards the leg side but he misses his flick and the ball goes off his pads towards the left of the keeper who dives and the batters steal a leg bye.
Another good length ball, this time on middle, worked towards the square leg region for a single.
Good length ball outside off, left alone by van der Dussen.

DRINKS! After the break the Englishmen have come out on all cylinders firing. They are constantly peppering the two South African batsmen with some chin music. Rassie van der Dussen has surpassed his fifty and would hope to continue the good work. Faf is just looking to stand there and grind it out. Can the English bowlers make some further inroads or the South African batsmen continue to fight it out in the middle? Intriguing session awaits us.

Ouch! Nasty, nasty delivery! Du Plessis has taken off his glove and is looking in some pain. Back of a length ball on middle, Faf looks to defend it off the back foot but he is hit on the glove. Looks like this has impacted his thumb more than anything else. The physio has come out to aid the South African skipper.
Another bouncer, this time Faf does well to evade it.
On the pads, worked towards the leg side for a single.
Good length delivery on middle and off, defended back towards the bowler.

Woah! What a bouncer that one and it has been theatrically left alone by van der Dussen too! A short ball, 141 kph, van der Dussen first thinks about playing at it but leaves it alone in the end and falls down in the process.
FOUR! Supreme drive! Full ball on off, van der Dussen comes forward and he drives this one through the cover region for a boundary.
Chris Woakes is back. 6-2-12-1, his numbers so far!
Back of a length ball on off, defended off the back foot.

Woah! What happened there? Broad bowls a length ball just outside the off pole line, the skipper chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump. The ball pitched and kept very low. Had that come in enough, it would have meant trouble for Faf. Replays roll in and show that it had come off the crack and that is why it stayed so low. England will keep looking for those now!
FOUR! Flicked away! On the pads, du Plessis plays a wristy shot towards the mid-wicket region and the ball races away to the fence.
Length ball on middle and leg, worked towards mid-wicket.
Length ball just outside off, left alone comfortably by the skipper.
Good length ball on middle and off, defended back towards the bowler.
Back of a length ball on middle, Faf hops and flicks it toward short mid-wicket where the fielder fumbles and the ball rolls towards mid-wicket which allows Faf to retain the strike.
Length and on off, Faf pushes the ball towards covers.
Du Plessis looks to tuck this length ball on middle and leg towards mid-wicket but he misses to take the blow on the thigh pad.
Outside off, Faf is happy leaving it.
Full on the pads, Rassie flicks it through mid-wicket and gets to the other end.
Length and outside off, Rassie guides it to gully.
Length and outside off, Faf punches it towards covers off the back foot.
Full ball on off, du Plessis pushes it back to the bowler.
Faf defends this length ball on off towards mid-wicket, who fumbles and the ball goes towards mid on.
Length ball on off, pushed back to the bowler off the back foot.
Length and outside off, van der Dussen taps it towards point and calls for a quick single. The batsmen get it easily.
Stuart starts his new spell with a length ball outside off, Rassie leaves it alone.
Change in bowling. Stuart Broad is back into the attack. 8 runs from his 4 overs today so far.
Full ball on off, Faf looks to defend it but the ball goes past the short leg towards deep square leg. The batsmen get a couple.
Length ball on off, Faf pushes the ball towards mid on off the back foot.
Full toss outside off, Rassie punches the ball through covers and gets to the other end.
Back of a length on off, van der Dussen hops and defends the ball towards point.
Third one in a row and Rassie ducks under it. The umpire penalizes Stokes by giving it as wide.
Another bouncer and Rassie goes for the pull only to miss it as the ball sails over him. Buttler looked excited but aborted the appeal as the umpire was not interested.
The short ball barrage continues as van der Dussen drops his wrists and sways away from the line.
Du Plessis shoulders arms to let this one through.

50 for Rassie van der Dussen! His 3rd Test half ton and he will be delighted with this one. A good length delivery bowled near the off pole line, Rassie pushes it towards mid off and takes a single to get to this milestone. However, he knows that his work is not even half done and he needs to convert this  into a big one if his side is to win this game.
On the pads again, flicked towards mid-wicket for a single.

Full ball on the pads, van der Dussen flicks it towards deep mid-wicket. The fielder in the deep runs to his left and cuts it off but the batters in the meantime take three quick runs. 100 up for South Africa with this too.
Length ball outside off, left alone by Rassie.
On the pads, played towards mid-wicket.
Full and on middle, flicked straight to the man at mid-wicket.
Bumper once again, Faf is quick to spot it and sways away from the line of the delivery.

NOT OUT! Faf survives. Bad review from Root there. Stokes bowls a length ball outside off, Faf looks to leave it but gets something on it on the way to the keeper. Buttler there takes the catch and immediately goes up in appeal. The umpire shakes his head. Root straightaway signals the 'T' because he definitely heard something there. The replays roll in to show that yes, it did hit something but it was not the bat or the glove, and instead it was the elbow. Faf continues to fight it out in the middle for himself and the team.
A huge appeal for caught behind has been turned down and England have taken the review straightaway. They think they have their man let's see what the replays have to say.
Full on the pads, van  der Dussen flicks it towards mid-wicket and takes a run.
Effort ball from Stokes there. It is angled right on the body. Rassie looks to pull it only to miss it. The ball sails past the ears of van der Dussen and into the mitts of the keeper.
Short of length ball outside off, van der Dussen hops and defends the ball off the back foot towards covers.
Short and on middle, van der Dussen pulls it all along the ground towards mid-wicket for a run.
Full and on off, Rasssie drives it towards mid on.
Short ball on middle and leg, van der Dussen ducks under it.
Length ball outside off, Rassie shoulders arms to it.

FOUR! Too full from Wood and van der Dussen pounces on it as he drives it past the bowler all along the ground showing the full face of the bat. No need to move there as the ball hurries to the long off fence.
Length ball on off, Rassie drives it towards covers.
Outside off, kept out off the front foot.
EDGED BUT SAFE! Length ball outside off, Faf looks to go for the drive through covers. But the ball takes the outside edge and rolls towards second slip.
Length ball on off, du Plessis looks to defend it but the ball takes the inside edge and hits Faf on the box.
Back of a length ball on off, Faf taps it towards short leg .
Length ball outside off, Faf lifts his bat and lets the ball through.
Back of a length and on off, Faf looks to flick it to the leg side. But extra bounce there means that the ball raps the gloves and rolls towards the off side.
On a length and on  off, Rassie taps it to covers off the back foot.
Fuller and outside off, Rassie drives it straight to covers.
Full ball on off, van der Dussen drives it back to the bowler.
Back of a length ball on middle, Rassie hops and defends it towards mid-wicket.
BEATEN! Beautiful delivery! Van der Dussen is squared up there as he looks to push this length ball outside off from the back foot.
Change of bats for Rassie van der Dussen.
Full and on off, Rassie drives if off the inside half of the bat towards mid on.
Mark Wood to partner Stokes first up in the second session.
Good length delivery on off, Faf lunges forward and defends it towards cover and calls his partner to wait.
Closer to the off stump, du Plessis blocks it with a straight bat.
Oh! Stokes hits the deck hard around off, it swings away just a hint. Faf looks to defend but gets beaten.
Stokes goes full and close to off stump, van der Dussen squeezes it to deep point for a single.
Calm and composed start from van der Dussen as he once again does not go after a length ball away from his stumps.
First ball of the post Lunch session and Stokes bowls it on a length outside off. It comes back in but Rassie is aware of his off stump and lets it be.

We are back after the Lunch Break. The South African batsmen Faf du Plessis and Rassie van der Dussen walk out to resume their innings. All eyes will be on the South African skipper as he has been short of runs. For England, Ben Stokes will start the session with the ball.
... Day 4, Session 2 ...

So, an important passage of play awaits us in Johannesburg. Can the South African batters hold fort and perform a miracle of some sorts or will England do what is looking inevitable? Join us at 1140 Local (0940 GMT) to find out!

29 overs, 90 runs and 2 wickets. That is what has happened in the morning session at Johannesburg on Day 4 and England will be happy with their performance so far. After a wicketless hour of play, Pieter Malan and Dean Elgar looked strong and confident. The Proteas were becoming hopeful that these two can stitch a good stand but right after the Drinks break, Woakes struck to dismiss Malan as he was caught in slips by Ben Stokes. Rassie van der Dussen walked in then, and he combined with the southpaw Dean Elgar to stitch a 50-run stand. However, right before the Lunch break, Stokes was again in the thick of things as he dismissed Elgar and England returned to the pavilion with smiles on their faces. South Africa would have loved if Elgar could have kept his wicket intact but it was not to be.
Floated on middle, du Plessis does well to block it back to the bowler. That will be LUNCH ON DAY 4!
Full ball on middle, du Plessis does well to turn it towards mid-wicket.
Tossed up on middle, Faf tucks it towards mid-wicket.
Full on middle, Faf defends it right under his eyes.
Full on leg stump, tucked past short leg and the batsmen take a run.
Tossed up on off, defended back to the bowler.
Hits the deck hard on the stumps, Faf du Plessis starts his innings with a back foot defense.

The skipper walks out to bat. Faf du Plessis is the new man in. He has been struggling for runs and there is a lot of pressure on him. His side needs him to be the messiah and take them out of troubled waters here. Can Faf deliver?

OUT! Caught! The budding stand has been broken and it is Ben Stokes who is once again in the thick of action. A very good ball this from the English all-rounder. He bends his back and bowls a very good short ball. The speed gun shows it is bowled at 136 kph but in real-time it looked quick. It is very close to Elgar's body and the ball skids off the surface. Elgar is hurried onto the pull and all he can do it lob it back to Stokes who takes an easy catch. Just when it looks like South Africa are onto something England put a brakes on it and dampen all the hopes. The pitch is hardly doing anything but Stokes once again shows why he is held in high regards and produces something special.
Good length ball just outside off, defended by Elgar back towards the bowler.
Bouncer on middle and off, Elgar ducks under it.
Outside off, left alone by Dean.
Length ball around off, defended back towards the bowler by Elgar.
Full on the pads, tucked to mid-wicket.

SIX! Van der Dussen is taking Root on. 50-run stand up between van der Dussen and Elgar. Rassie skips down the track and hoicks one over the fence at mid-wicket. The fielder there is a mere spectator as the ball sails way over him and into the stands.
FOUR! Now van der Dussen plays the conventional sweep and finds the fence. Full and on middle this time, Rassie sweeps it through fine leg and the ball meets the fence in no time.
Tossed up on off, kept out.
Root bowls one on the pads and Rassie tucks it to leg slip.

FOUR BYES! The trap was set there. Root tossed one up on middle and leg, van der Dussen tries to tuck it but the ball just about bounce a tad and it evades the keeper and the leg slip fielder on its way towards fine leg. The umpire gives it as byes.
On the pads, flicked towards mid-wicket for a single.
FOUR! Driven away! Full ball on off, van der Dussen comes forward and drives this ball through the cover region for a boundary.
Fullish ball on off, pushed to the man at mid off.
Good length delivery on middle and off, defended.
On the pads, flicked towards deep square leg for a single by Elgar.
Full ball on middle and leg, defended towards the bowler.

FOUR! Three boundaries in the over for van der Dussen. Rassie is getting a move on here. Introduction of spin has helped the batter there as he once again reverse sweeps it to find the fence at third man.

FOUR! Tossed up on off, van der Dussen dances down the track and flicks this one. He hits it just over the leaping short mid-wicket fielder there and the ball has enough in it to roll over the boundary cushions at mid-wicket.
Tossed up on middle, tucked to short leg.
Tossed up on off, pushed back to the bowler.

FOUR! Beautifully played there by van der Dussen. Root bowls a full ball on middle, Rassie sees the length and promptly gets in position to reverse sweep it. He gets the placement right and the ball races to the third man fence for a boundary.
Tossed up on off, pushed towards covers.
Time for some spin. Skipper Joe Root to try his luck now.
Full ball on off, Rassie drives it towards mid off and keeps the strike.
Outside off, pushed to covers for a single.
Length ball on off, Elgar pushes the ball off the back foot towards point.
Length ball on off, played off the front foot there by Elgar.
Short ball on off, Dean ducks under it.
Back of a length ball on middle, Elgar blocks it back to the bowler.
Full ball on off, defended off the back foot there by van der Dussen.
Length and around off, Rassie blocks it off the front foot.
Once again, outside off, van der Dussen leaves it for the keeper.
Angling away outside off, Rassie lets it go through to the keeper.
Full and angled away outside off, Rassie looks to lay bat on ball but he misses it.
Full on middle, Rassie flicks it straight to the man at mid-wicket.
Last ball of the over. Elgar keeps it out.
Elgar drives this full ball outside off towards point.
Dean defends this length delivery off the front foot and onto the ground.
Elgar blocks one off the back foot there.
Length ball on off, defended off the back foot.
Length ball outside off, further going away. Elgar lets it be.
Time for Ben Stokes to have a go with the ball.

FOUR! Curran errs in line and dishes one onto the pads of van der Dussen. He just flicks it off the back foot and the ball rolls over the mid-wicket fence. The fielder in the deep cannot do anything there.
Back of a length ball on off, kept out off the back foot towards cover.
Van der Dussen just taps this length ball off the front foot towards covers.
On the pads of Elgar. He just flicks it through fine leg and gets an easy single there.
Elgar pushes this length ball straight towards covers.
BEATEN ! Curran makes the ball curve away from the forward push of Elgar. Dean is lucky there to not edge it.
Rassie does well to keep this length ball out off the back foot.
Van der Dussen once again pushes this length delivery on off towards the bowler.
Length ball outside off, pushed back to the bowler off the back foot.
Back of a length ball on off, Rassie looks to pull but is beaten to get rapped on the thigh pads.
Rassie pushes the ball off the back foot towards the bowler.
Length ball outside off, pushed to covers off the front foot.
Outside off, left alone.
Elgar keeps out this length ball outside off.

FOUR! Elgar has played that superbly. Dean pushes this length ball outside off straight down the ground and the ball beats the dive of the mid off fielder running to his left and it rolls towards the long off fence for a boundary. 50 comes up with this for South Africa.
Elgar blocks this length ball off the back foot and towards the covers.

Oh! That beats Elgar. He would have had his heart in his mouth. He looks to poke this length ball outside off but the ball sneaks past the outside edge and the ball lands into the mitts of the keeper.
Length ball outside off, Elgar defends the ball off the outside half of the bat towards covers.
Outside off, driven towards point for a couple.
Outside off, pushed to the man at cover.
BEATEN! Beauty of a nut there. Rassie is lured into poking this length ball outside off. Luckily he does not edge it behind.
Oh! The inside edge there. Rassie looks to defend this length ball off the back foot only to get an inside edge onto his pads.
FOUR! Short ball on middle and Rassie takes the full toll of it. He just pulls it with disdain and the ball races to the mid-wicket fence for a boundary.
Good length ball on off, Rassie blocks it off the back foot and into the ground.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Wide! Bouncer on middle and leg, Elgar ducks as it is way too high.
Woah! Jaffa by Curran! Bowls a back of a length delivery just outside off, and this time gets it to nip back in. Elgar looks to defend but the ball cuts him in half and oohs and aahs all around.
Full ball on the off pole line, defended back towards the bowler.
Outside off, Dean leaves this one alone.
Length ball on middle and off, Elgar defends it towards the man at mid off.
Good length ball on middle and off, defended back towards the bowler.
Sam Curran is back on.

Another huge appeal but this time the umpire shakes his head. Very full on off and it nips back in. Rassie looks to play but gets a feather on it onto the pads. The English players are once again excited but this time the umpire is not.

NOT OUT! Rassie survives. Good referral by the South African no. 3! He lives to fight another day. Good length ball pitching around off, van der Dussen looks to defend but misses. The ball hits him high on the pads of his back leg. The English players go up in a huge appeal and the umpire raises his finger. Rassie has a word with his partner and then signals the 'T'. Replay rolls in and first Ultra Edge confirms that there is no bat involved. Ball Tracker then rolls in and it shows that the ball is pitching in line, the impact though is Umpire's call. Then time to see whether the ball is hitting the stumps or not. It shows that the ball was going over the stumps.
Review time! Rassie van der Dussen is the man in question. The umpire has adjudged him out and it looks close to the naked eye. The Ball Tracker rolls in and shows that this is going OVER the stumps.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Outside off, left alone.
Good length ball on off, van der Dussen blocks it.
Rassie van der Dussen is the new man in.

OUT! CAUGHT! Malan departs and maybe it is a commentator's curse after all. Just as we said the openers cannot lose their concentration, Malan loses his focus, maybe the break in play brought about his downfall. Woakes is the man who has drawn first blood here. Full and wide outside off, Malan goes chasing after it like a kid chasing candy. He ends up getting a thick outside edge which goes to the right of Ben Stokes. You cannot keep him out of the game and he takes a good catch. Catching practice at slip for Big Ben. The steady opening stand has been taken down.

Drinks! A good solid hour for South Africa but they cannot afford to lose their concentration here. It is a long, long ask and the pair of Malan and Elgar need to keep on going for a big period of time. England will not be too disappointed with not getting a wicket in the first hour of play. They have plenty of runs to play with but they will look to strike at least a couple before the end of this session.
Good length ball on off, Malan pushes it wide of cover for a run. He will keep the strike.
Short ball, Malan ducks under it.

FOUR! Classic cover drive. You can keep on watching this shot on loop and you will continue to admire this every single time. Full around off, Malan gets on his front foot and leans into the cover drive. The outfield is quick so the fielder has no chance stopping that.
Outside off, Malan lunges forward and lets it carry to the keeper.
Good length ball on middle and leg, Malan once again plays it well as he glances it onto the ground towards short leg.
On the hips of Malan, he tucks it on the bounce to short leg.
Length ball on off, Malan pushes it wide of cover for one.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Woakes goes full on off, PM once again uses a dead bat to see it off.
On a length on off, Pieter defends this.
Fuller on off, Malan blocks it.
Absolute peach to end the over. Wood hits the deck hard outside off, it looks to be coming in with the angle but straightens up as it comes off the pitch. Elgar looks to defend but gets squared up.
After going short on the previous two balls, Wood goes very full on off. Elgar defends it to the left of the bowler. Wood goes to ground and gets his hand to it and deflects the ball to mid on.
Another short ball. This one is outside off and Dean sways away from it in a better way.
Bouncer! A very well-directed one by Wood. Elgar ducks under it awkwardly but no harm done.
Length delivery on off stump this time, Elgar defends this towards mid off.
FOUR! Just pure timing on this one! Good length delivery around off, Elgar hangs on his back foot and uses the pace of Wood and just taps it through point for a boundary.
FOUR! Another back of a length ball on off, Malan rocks back and cuts and it goes just above the man at gully and into the third man fence.
Back of a length ball outside off, left alone.
Outside off, Malan does not fiddle with it and leaves it alone.

This time a louder appeal by England but again turned down! Good length ball just outside off, Malan looks to defend but fails to do so. The ball lobs towards the man at silly point who takes the catch and appeals. The umpire again shakes his head as he reckons this one has come off the pads of Malan. England opt against taking the review. Ball Tracker comes in and shows it was hitting the pad and the impact was outside off.
Length ball outside off, left alone.
Good length ball outside off, Malan looks to bend and defend but he misses the ball and is hit on the thigh pad.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Length ball on middle and off, defended.

Another appeal turned down! Length ball down the leg side, Elgar looks to flick this one fine but fails to do so. The ball deflects off his thigh pad towards Pope at short leg. He takes the catch and the England players appeal but the umpire turns it down. Replays confirm it did not hit the bat nor the glove.
Another length ball which is outside off, Elgar does not fiddle with it.
Another one outside off, left alone.
Length ball outside off, Elgar leaves this one alone.

Outside off, Elgar leaves this one alone and gets through the over. South Africa have scored 25 runs at the end of the the first 10 overs of the day, but more importantly, they have not lost a single wicket so far.
Back of a length ball on the off side, defended towards the man at point for a single.
Length ball outside off, left alone.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot.
Another one on the pads, played towards the man at mid-wicket.
On the pads, flicked towards the man at square leg.
Change from both the ends. Chris Woakes replaces Sam Curran from the other end.
Full ball on middle and off, Malan pushes it down the ground past the man at mid on and the batters take a couple to end the over.
Bouncer down the leg side, Malan ducks and lets it go.
Length ball on off, played towards the man at point.
Full ball on middle and off, defended back towards Wood.
Good length ball on middle and leg, defended towards the man at short leg.
Good running! Wood starts with a full ball on off, Elgar plays it with soft hands towards the off side and takes a very quick single. Intent!
First bowling change of the game. The hero with the ball from the first innings, actually the English hero and antagonist for South Africa in this game so far, Mark Wood is into the attack.
Another one on off and fuller in length, defended towards the man at mid off.
Fullish delivery around off, pushed to the man at mid off.
Once again on the pads, played towards square leg again but this time just a run.
FOUR! Well played but a bad ball! On the pads of Elgar, he flicks this one in the gap near square leg and the ball races away to the fence.
On the pads of Malan, he flicks this one towards the mid-wicket region and the batters take a single.
Good length ball on off, Malan plays a beautiful shot through the cover-point region and the batters take a couple.
Length ball outside off, left alone.
Length ball on off, defended towards the off side and Malan rotates strike.

Appeal turned down! Good length ball just outside off, coming in. Malan looks to defend this off the front foot but misses to get hit on the back leg's thigh pad. The England players appeal but nothing from the umpire. The impact looks outside off and Ball Tracker confirms it.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Another good length ball on the off side, this time Elgar defends it towards the off side with soft hands and takes a single.

Stuart Broad produces something special as soon as he comes around the wicket. Good length delivery just outside off, angling in. It pitches and nips away. Elgar looks to play at it but is completely beaten.
On the stumps, Malan defends it with a dead bat.
Full and swinging away from off, Elgar looks to defend but the ball takes the outside edge and rolls to third a for a single.
Full on off, Elgar pushes it to mid off.

Almost chopped on. Length ball just outside off. Elgar looks to cut but the ball is too close to the stumps and his body. He still goes for it, he ends up chopping it behind and luckily for him and his team the ball does not go onto hit the stumps.
Full on middle, Elgar strokes it to mid on.
Good length delivery outside off, Elgar lets it carry to the keeper.
Follows the boundary with a calm push to mid off.

FOUR! Beautiful drive from Malan. Slightly overpitched on off and middle, Malan gets in a good position on his front foot and drives it with class through mid off for a boundary. This will give him a lot of confidence.
Full on off, Malan pushes it to mid on.
Broad goes full and closer to the off pole. Malan defends it with surety.
Good length delivery outside off, asking Malan to have a crack but he calmly leaves it alone.

Huge appeal for LBW but probably going down the leg side. Full on middle and leg, it goes with the angle. Malan looks to flick but misses. There is a huge appeal from the English players but the umpire turns it down.
Good length delivery on middle and off, defended towards the off side by Elgar.
Length ball on middle and leg, Elgar looks to defend but is hit on the thigh pad.

EDGED AND FOUR! Good length ball down the leg side, Elgar looks to work it towards that side but the ball goes off the leading edge behind the man at point and into the fence for a boundary. First boundary of the innings.
Defended off the back foot towards the man at cover-point.
Good length ball on middle and leg, pushed towards the man at mid on.

Jaffa! What a delivery by Curran! A length delivery just outside off, angling in. It pitches and then goes away as Elgar looks to play at it. He is completely squared up but the ball beats his outside edge.
Good length delivery outside off, Malan leaves it alone to finish the over.
Length delivery outside off, left alone by Malan again.
First runs of the day! On the pads of Malan, he flicks this one towards square leg and gets a couple.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
Fuller ball on the off pole line, Malan looks to defend but the ball goes off the outer half towards the man at point all along the ground.
Length ball outside off to start the over by Malan, he leaves this one alone.
Outside off, left alone by Elgar.
Length ball outside off, Elgar defends this one towards the off side.
Good length ball on middle and off, Elgar defends this one onto the pitch and the ball goes above Curran and the man from mid off runs to his left to gather the ball.
Length ball outside off, left alone by Elgar.
Curran goes fuller, he defends this one towards the man at mid off.
Length ball on off to start with by Curran, Elgar defends it off the back foot towards the man at point.
Sam Curran to partner Stuart Broad from the other end.

Ohh! Good delivery to end the over! Length ball on off, angling in, Malan offers no stroke but the ball comes in too much and is hit near the box. End of a good over as England look to attack the Proteas straightaway.
Good length ball attacking the middle pole, Malan defends this one towards the man at mid on.
Fuller one on off by Broad, Malan pushes this one towards the man at cover.
Another full ball attacking the off pole, Malan shuffles across and defends this towards the mid-wicket fielder.
Back of a length ball on middle and off, left alone by Pieter Malan.
Broad starts the day with a full length ball attacking the stumps, Malan does well to defend this ball out.
